channel.title: Lead Green blog
channel.description: The energy behind the token. Public measurements of GPU energy per million output tokens, and what they mean for the people who buy, run and audit AI.

item.title: How much energy does an AI query use?
item.dc:creator: Prem Naraindas
item.description: One answer from a busy 32B model costs about 0.040 Wh of GPU energy; Google says 0.24 Wh per median prompt. Both are right. Here is why.

item.title: What is watt-hours per million tokens, and why not joules per token?
item.dc:creator: Prem Naraindas
item.description: The unit behind the index: what Wh/M counts, what it leaves out, how it converts to kWh, carbon and the meter, and why joules per token became watt-hours.

item.title: Why an idle GPU wastes energy: the concurrency ladder
item.dc:creator: Prem Naraindas
item.description: Same model, same two H100 cards: 7.1× in GPU energy per token between a running batch of 8 and 256. Why the under-used card is the expensive one.

item.title: What a million tokens costs in watt-hours
item.dc:creator: Prem Naraindas
item.description: What the public measurements say a million output tokens takes in GPU watt-hours, and why a busy server uses a fraction of the energy of a quiet one.
